newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Hanson's Imperial looks to export.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Hanson's Imperial looks to export.

text.p: Imperial Tobacco Group Plc, the British tobacco company in the process of demerging from Hanson Plc, is looking to build on a history of cost-cutting with a strategy based on exports.
"Ours is an export-led strategy," Imperial Tobacco chief executive Gareth Davis told Reuters.

Speaking after the mailing of demerger details for Imperial and chemicals group Millennium Chemicals Inc, Davies said Imperial's float with approximately 1.1 billion stg of debt was within market expectations.
Davis said the valuation of Imperial, which will be effective from October 1, was "something the market will decide at the end of the day".
He stressed the company's cash-generative nature, saying that in its 1994/95 year it converted 99 percent of its operating profit into cash, generating some 345 million stg.

Davis said in the period of ownership by Hanson, the company had improved its cigarette-manufacturing productivity by 195 percent and said its return on sales figure of 46 percent was the highest of any of its competitors.
Imperial, whose brands include John Player Special, Superkings and Embassy, has increased its share of the British cigarette market to 38 percent from below 33 percent in 1990.
This, however, is in the context of a market which has decelined by two percent per year, leading the company to focus more on overseas.
Davis said the export strategy was firstly to achieve a higher penetration of continental European markets and secondly to expand in the massive Asia-Pacific market.
"It's early days yet but Greater China offers significant opportunities for us," he said.
In Europe outside Britain, Imperial has increased its share to four percent from 0.5 percent over the past 18 months and has a 27 percent share of the Irish market.

The company, which announced the appointment of three non-executive directors, is currently investing 35 million stg in new plant at its Nottingham, central England, cigarette factory which Davis said will enable it to produce and pack 14,000 cigarettes per minute.
